title: Regression horizon snapshot & ops checklist — 2026-04-05
body:
Purpose:
This note is a compact, actionable snapshot of current onboarding regression behavior for the last two weeks (2026-03-22 -> 2026-04-04). It mixes telemetry highlights, concrete example failures from promptsets, and a prioritized ops checklist so SRE/serving/AM teams can act quickly. Intended audience: applied-ml triage lead, serving runtime oncall, infra, and the onboarding PM.

Executive summary:
- Overall quality delta: cohort-average F1 on core onboarding promptsets down 6.4% vs baseline (baseline = model-variant v2.3-stable).
- Top customer-visible failures: hallucination on short factual queries; tokenization edge-cases for long code snippets; price-critical truncation for financial templates.
- Immediate impact: 3 onboarding customers flagged (support tickets opened) — two escalated to CSMs.
- Recommended immediate actions: rollback lightweight kernel tweak in canary (infra) + re-enable prefix-KV caching for session-class workloads (serving runtime).

Key telemetry (high-level):
- Promptset coverage: 1,240 unique prompts across 12 onboarding kits.
- Regression rate: 7.8% of promptset-items crossed failure thresholds (precision drop > 5% or hallucination score > 0.25).
- Latency changes: median token latency unchanged; 95p tail increased 12% for long-context (> 4k tokens) flows.
- Cost delta: per-token GPU time up ~4% for the experimental quant path on dedicated pools.
- Alert triggers: MLREG-318 (precision drift) triggered at 2026-03-29 04:12 UTC.

Top failure modes (examples + quick notes):
1) Short factual hallucination (HF-01)
   - Symptoms: Confident but incorrect facts on 1–2 sentence queries (e.g., "When did company X IPO?" -> wrong year).
   - Example prompt: "When did Acme Robotics go public?"
   - Root-hypothesis: model-variant undertrained on updated knowledge cutoff plus temperature profile shift in canary config.
   - Immediate mitigation: pin temperature to 0.0 for factual promptsets; add deterministic fallback to 'knowledge-check' policy. Owner: Jian Li. Due: 2026-04-06.

2) Code tokenization anomalies (CT-02)
   - Symptoms: Collapsed tokens in long code blocks causing parse-failures in downstream tooling.
   - Example prompt: long JS snippet with embedded template literals -> returned invalid syntax.
   - Hypothesis: tokenizer bpe vocab mismatch from modified tokenizer mapping in model build.
   - Mitigation: revert tokenizer mapping patch in canary, add targeted unit test (sample snippet set). Owner: Riley Thompson. Due: 2026-04-07.

3) Truncation in financial templates (TR-03)
   - Symptoms: Generated summaries drop last clause when input near 6k tokens.
   - Hypothesis: KV-cache eviction policy shifted; batching now forces earlier context eviction.
   - Mitigation: temporary priority pinning of session-class requests to non-batched lanes; increase KV retention threshold by 2 tokens for affected models. Owner: Samir Gupta (SRE + serving). Due: 2026-04-06.

4) Reranking regressions for multi-turn intent routing (RR-04)
   - Symptoms: Intent classifier ranks correct intent 3rd instead of 1st for 9% of multi-intent prompts.
   - Quick fix: reapply last successful reranker weights, schedule retrain with augmented promptset. Owner: Elena Morales. Due: 2026-04-12.

5) Eval coverage blind spots (EC-05)
   - Symptoms: Several failures surfaced by customers are absent from onboarding promptsets (legal disclaimers, non-English short forms).
   - Action: expand promptset coverage by 120 high-impact prompts flagged by CSMs. Owner: Nadia Karim. Due: 2026-04-09.

Triage notes & how we verified failures:
- Verification pipeline: sampled failing items, ran against v2.3-stable + v2.4-canary, and computed delta metrics (precision/recall, hallucination(semantic) score, tokenization error rate).
- For hallucinations we used human spot-check on top 50 high-confidence failures (3 raters, majority vote).
- Code tokenization tests reproduced locally with our tokenizer unit-test harness (infra PR linked).

Prioritized action checklist (immediate -> short-term -> mid-term):
Immediate (0–72h):
- [ ] Revert tokenizer mapping change in canary (infra rollback). Owner: Riley Thompson. Due: 2026-04-07.
- [ ] Pin temperature 0.0 for factual promptsets under onboarding flow; add deterministic fallback. Owner: Jian Li. Due: 2026-04-06.
- [ ] Re-enable prefix-KV caching for session-class lanes in canary region (us-west1). Owner: Samir Gupta. Due: 2026-04-05 (urgent).
- [ ] Notify CSMs on progress + send interim note to affected customers. Owner: Elena Morales. Due: 2026-04-05.

Short-term (3–14 days):
- [ ] Add 120 prompts to onboarding promptset, prioritized by customer escalation. Owner: Nadia Karim. Due: 2026-04-09.
- [ ] Backfill reranker training data and kick retrain (with holdout evaluation). Owner: Elena Morales + Applied ML. Due: 2026-04-12.
- [ ] Add tokenizer regression tests into CI and a canary gate for tokenizer diffs. Owner: Riley Thompson. Due: 2026-04-14.
- [ ] Deploy KV-cache retention policy tune to dedicated pools (A/B test). Owner: Samir Gupta. Due: 2026-04-13.

Mid-term (2–6 weeks):
- [ ] Model-variant audit: run knowledge-cutoff drift analysis across our model catalog and set variant-level policies. Owner: Applied ML leads. Due: 2026-05-10.
- [ ] Expand the onboarding evaluation harness to include multilingual legal templates and finance templates. Owner: Product + Applied ML. Due: 2026-05-03.

Quick experiments to run (low effort, high signal):
- Experiment A: Temperature sweep for factual buckets (0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.2) with 5k samples. Metric: hallucination rate.
- Experiment B: Mini-A/B for prefix-KV retention + batch-size cap for long-context sessions (target: reduce 95p latency tail by 20%).
- Experiment C: Tokenizer patch test against curated code-snippet corpus (1000 examples).

Operational checklist for safe rollouts (for infra + serving):
- Canary gating: ensure canary reflects full config (tokenizer, kernel selection, quant paths).
- Alerting: MLREG threshold lowered to 4% delta for onboarding promptsets while active mitigations are in-flight.
- Runbook update: append KB article "hallucination-fallbacks" to oncall runbooks and link to CSM escalation steps.
- Postmortem trigger: if customer-facing escalations > 5 within 7 days, open P0 incident.

Risks and open questions:
- Reverting tokenizer may mask an underlying model-build issue; need to trace build artifacts in the CI artifact store. (Jenkins job #build-8799 referenced).
- Cache retention fix may increase GPU memory pressure on dedicated pools — coordinate with capacity planning.
- Some prompt failures are due to data freshness (knowledge cutoff). How many customers require dynamic knowledge injection vs static model updates?

Handoff notes for next 48h:
- Oncall (Samir): prioritize KV-cache revert and watch 95p latency.
- Infra (Riley): schedule tokenizer rollback and block new model builds until tests pass.
- Applied ML (Jian + Elena): pin temperature for factual promptsets and prepare reranker data.
- CSM/Support (Nadia): collect concrete customer examples and confirm whether added prompts match problem cases.

Appendix — sample failing prompts (sanitized):
- "When did Acme Robotics IPO?" -> model returned 2015 (incorrect; correct: 2012).
- Long JS snippet with nested template literal causing unexpected "�" tokens at generation boundary.
- Financial summary prompt (5.9k tokens) where final clause "...net operating cash flow" missing from result.

Next steps / meeting cadence:
- Daily 15m triage standup (sticky) until immediate checklist closed. Owner: Elena Morales. Start: 2026-04-05 09:30 PT.
- Deep-dive retro on 2026-04-13 to capture root causes and update onboarding eval harness.

Notes / rough thoughts (brain-dump):
- Consider a rapid "knowledge patch" service for non-core customers to inject recent facts while we handle model re-syncs.
- Could the quant path increase explain hallucination behaviour? Track quant-specific hallucination deltas separately in the next run.
- We need smoother telemetry linking from tokenization errors back to exact build commits — maybe include commit hash in generated model metadata.

If you want: I can extract the top 50 failing items and upload as a separate CSV for MLREG triage (recommended).

-- Elena
__notes: internal: created from triage run and human checks; intended to be iterative (add to page as actions complete)
